S50.01.needs: a browser that supports speech synthesis, with at least one system voice
S50.01.note: The Read message aloud item appears only when the browser supports speech and the reply has readable text; I did not trace whether the More message actions button is hover-only on desktop.
steps: Sign in to the AGI Web app and open a conversation that has an assistant reply.
Move the pointer over the assistant reply, then click the button labelled More message actions.
Click Read message aloud in the menu.
Look for the reply being spoken aloud, and for the same menu item now reading Stop reading message while it plays.
S50.01.where: Chat, under an assistant reply > More message actions > Read message aloud

S50.02.needs: a browser with at least one system voice; the row shows a message instead if the browser has no voices
S50.02.note: There is no separate language picker for read-aloud; the language comes with the chosen voice. The menu entry that opens Settings was not traced to its exact label, so the first step names the General tab only.
steps: Sign in, open Settings, and choose the General tab.
Scroll to the Preferences heading and find the row Backup read-aloud voice.
Open the drop-down labelled Backup read-aloud voice and choose a voice; each option shows its name and language code in brackets, and Browser default is the first option.
Click Preview next to the drop-down and listen; compare the voice and language with what you chose.
S50.02.where: Settings > General > Preferences > Backup read-aloud voice

S50.03.needs: a browser with speech synthesis support; the row is hidden when speech is not supported
S50.03.note: The speed applies to browser read-aloud only (rates in apps/web/shared/stores/web-settings-store.ts); the separate Live voice pace row in the same section is for live voice conversations. The menu entry that opens Settings was not traced to its exact label.
steps: Sign in, open Settings, and choose the General tab.
Scroll to the Preferences heading and find the row Read-aloud speed.
Click Slow, Normal or Fast; the chosen button is shown as pressed.
Open an assistant reply, use Read message aloud, and compare the pace with the Normal setting.
